A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MonoAttn-Transducer research despite the changed title and layout. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuST-C speech-to-text and CVSS-C speech-to-speech experiments, prior-choice ablations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original translation experiments, non-monotonicity subset results, and training-time and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The posterior-alignment calculation, expected monotonic attention, prior distributions, chunk synchronization, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendix A also retains the same offline pretraining and streaming finetuning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MuST-C English–German and English–Spanish speech-to-text translation and CVSS-C French–English speech-to-speech translation. Streaming/offline scenarios and the non-monotonicity subsets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds LSG as a comparator in Figure 2, with a visible English–German result curve. Existing comparators remain. AlignAtt is newly discussed, but no identifiable plotted or tabulated AlignAtt results establish its participation in the reported evaluation.

E3.justification: Speech-to-speech Table 3 replaces AL reporting with LAAL and adds StartOffset. Table 2 switches to LAAL, although baseline and posterior-model LAAL results already appeared in v1's appendix. Model configurations, chunk sizes, preprocessing, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the entire quantitative prior-choice sensitivity study from v1 Section 6.1/Table 4 and all four uniform-prior alignment examples from Appendix D. This eliminates direct evidence testing robustness to prior choice. The non-monotonicity subset analysis, efficiency analysis, and diagonal-prior examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The reporting practice remains single-point results.

E6.justification: The principal BLEU, COMET, ASR-BLEU, and efficiency results remain unchanged. CAAT curves are revised, LSG results and prior-variant LAAL values are added, and uniform-prior ablation results are removed. Speech Table 3 replaces tabulated AL of 153/118 ms with LAAL of 984/918 ms and StartOffset of 1520/1491 ms for Transducer/MonoAttn-Transducer; these are different metrics, not performance changes.

T1.justification: The forward-backward derivation, posterior alignment, attention expectations, prior definitions, and chunk-synchronization mathematics are retained. v2 Equation 10 explicitly restates the existing use of the estimated context vector in the predictor; it introduces no new derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an efficient posterior-based monotonic-attention mechanism that improves Transducer handling of non-monotonic streaming generation. The revised title, abstract, and conclusion preserve the contribution's meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly acknowledges AlignAtt's superior performance above two seconds of delay and states that this work primarily targets shorter delays. Existing explanations of chunk-size effects, posterior alignment, computational costs, and low-latency limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the preprocessing, curriculum, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information. The code and preprocessing-resource links and SimulEval version are unchanged. The added comparator descriptions supply no corresponding implementation configurations.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion for LSG, AlignAtt, and Fuzzy Alignments in Directed Acyclic Graph for Non-Autoregressive Machine Translation. This modestly extends the research context while retaining the existing positioning against Transducer and streaming attention methods.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract is shortened, and local wording and affiliation information are revised. The prior-choice subsection is removed and an Impact Statement added, but most exposition and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensively repositioned and resized displays. v1's architecture schematic, prior-choice table, and four uniform-prior figures disappear. The comparison plot gains LSG, and the speech-results table gains another latency row.

improvement.justification: The added LSG comparison and latency measures modestly broaden reporting. However, v2 removes the quantitative and visual evidence for prior-choice robustness while retaining that assertion in Appendix D. Section 5.4 also retains the 118 ms AL discussion without reconciling it with Table 3's replacement metrics. These losses weaken evidential support and reporting clarity, while the core method and results remain intact.
